comparisonAssessment.sufficientFor: Binding these concrete helpers to matching complete executable/data/load-command bytes except the 16-byte UUID payload and trailing LC_CODE_SIGNATURE allocation. All other bytes and all load-command offset/size fields remain equal. Strict signatures verify; CodeDirectory security metadata and other signature slots independently match after excluding the verified code-page hash table.
comparisonAssessment.signatureAllocationPrecision: LC_CODE_SIGNATURE reserves 848 bytes, while the Apple Superblob declares 826. The remaining 22 allocated tail bytes are nonzero and included in the exclusion. This allocation is contained in the non-executable __LINKEDIT tail and overlaps no other file-backed segment. The report does not describe the excluded 848 bytes as only the structured 826-byte Superblob.

comparisonAssessment.parentComparatorReview: The JS implementation masks the correct two ranges for the actual three valid files and preserves all other bytes. Its general parser checks are narrower (JS numeric segment conversion, minimal signature superblob checks); the independent parser adds exact integer bounds, segment containment, signature index/slot bounds and policy metadata comparison. Adequate for this bounded code/data equivalence claim.
comparisonAssessment.independentParserObservation: The first read-only parser attempt assumed the signature allocation tail must be zero. Actual codesign-valid files contain 22 nonzero bytes after the declared Superblob. That assumption was removed, actual allocation/structured lengths and tail hashes are reported, and no executable/helper test was rerun.
